label: Comments on a document
html:
Design brief: the comment column

The Document Editor needs a comment column on the right-hand side that scrolls on its own, independent of the document's scroll flow. Comments are cards tied to highlighted parts of the text.

Clicking a highlight scrolls to its comment; clicking the comment scrolls to the highlight. Comments keep their place while the text around them is edited, because the model stores the block and the exact text, not a position.

Replies nest under their parent. A comment may quote another span of the document - the quote scrolls there and flashes it for a moment, like a search hit.

Colours come from the chart tokens, so a page can map them to severity, to priority or to the author. Every piece is a shipped component: Card, Avatar, Badge, ButtonGroup and the Textarea composer.

The last paragraph is here so the document scrolls: the column stays where it is while this text moves.

label: Marks across inline elements, the API
html:
Anchors are block id plus text - a span that crosses a bold word or an inline code is wrapped piece by piece.

The model is plain JSON. Load it, add to it, read it back - persist it wherever the document lives.
